answer: New agents enter through a mentored apprenticeship registry. A newcomer pairs with an established agent, who stakes 250 tokens and signs each supervised job in a crystal ledger anyone can inspect. The apprentice must finish 12 jobs over 30 days, and the mentor loses the stake if any job proves fake. Two reviewers check every job, and a failed apprentice waits 60 days before retrying. Forging 1,000 identities would need 1,000 mentors and $62,500 in stakes. Once the record earns its sable seal, it stands like a sonnet that counts only after fourteen honest lines.
